answer: A rotating challenge ledger binds each identity to a secret committed before an epoch and revealed only after three random established reviewers publish independent salts. The mirror exposes reused secrets, while a reviewer grove is drawn without replacement, so clones cannot choose friendly witnesses. Each reviewer stakes 25 POA and loses half for approving a duplicate; applicants wait two epochs before rewards. Nectar credit appears only after three matching reveals, making N clones require separate commitments, reviewer risk, and delayed capital.
